description: Literature, ancient history, yoga, political history, biology, transport, Orwell, art, music and philosophy lead into later questions on airships, cryptozoology, geography and Shakespearean language within the same broadcaster season.

s08e01.description: Dickens’s A Christmas Carol, moats, military commands, concrete, Amazon’s Kindle and Paris Saint-Germain all appear before Milton’s Paradise Lost adds literary scale to the episode.

s08e02.description: Hula hoops, the meaning of clumsy, pescatarians, Scarborough, fluoride toothpaste and newsreader Sophie Raworth all appear before ancient history eventually reaches Babylon.

s08e03.description: Ping-pong and the conga begin a question set that later stretches into yoga with Downward Facing Dog. The episode’s subjects move from table sport to dance to a pose whose name remains far more memorable than most anatomy terminology.

s08e04.description: Dua Lipa and Elton John’s Cold Heart, Britain’s 2012 ‘Super Saturday’ Olympic champions and Australia’s dominance of world opal reserves all appear before twentieth-century political history introduces the phrase Black Power.

s08e05.description: The Mary Rose, Lusitania, Titanic and Bismarck are placed in sinking chronology before carrier pigeons, the Wars of the Roses, bicycle spokes, emulsion paint and Earth’s orbit all appear. Biology eventually contributes parthenogenesis.

s08e06.description: Skyscanner, Pixar’s hopping desk lamp, nitrogen in crisp packets, the French name for Aquarius and the order of rainbow colours all feature before the questions travel to New York’s Grand Central Station.

s08e07.description: Birds are compared by average weight before berets, mulled wine, string quartets, Madonna’s Vogue and the Royal Shakespeare Company appear. Orwellian literature eventually opens the door to Room 101.

s08e08.description: Ouija boards, ASAP, Paul Simon’s 50 Ways to Leave Your Lover, Britain’s change from burgundy to blue passports and Burns Night’s haggis, neeps and tatties all appear before Venetian painting brings in Canaletto.

s08e09.description: Joel Dommett’s celebrity run covers Steps, Dalmatians, Hawaiian pizza, TNT, Las Vegas and the submarine drama Vigil before the questions eventually reach the Neapolitan song O Sole Mio.

s08e10.description: Jo Brand encounters Christmas crackers, papier-mâché, Dover sole, The Social Network, pumice and the Ponzi scheme before the ladder eventually reaches Sartre’s famously cheerful line, ‘Hell is other people’.

s08e11.description: A bird’s bill, engagement rings, whistleblowing, recommended retail prices and sixteen-digit debit-card numbers all appear in the same broadcast before the question set reaches the Hindenburg and its place in airship history.

s08e12.description: Strictly and Britain’s Got Talent judging, the Bastille, the Stanley Cup and Britain’s native snakes all feature before the notorious Patterson-Gimlin film drags Bigfoot into the hot seat.

s08e13.description: Hamlet, Shaun the Sheep and the phalanges of hands and feet precede the wonderfully neat Tango/Tonga anagram question. French menu terminology then adds food cooked en brochette to the episode’s linguistic pile.

s08e14.description: Jools Holland’s celebrity run moves from spoons and Listerine to signing on the dotted line, PE with Joe and Hitchcock’s Psycho. Shakespeare later supplies ‘method in my madness’, an unusually apt phrase for the surrounding trivia.
